column1: # Bounded Korean count-context expansion; see docs/korean-counters.md.
# Complete left tokens require matching streaming boundaries.
# Right cues are prefixes of the next word after an optional registered particle.
# Longest noun cues guard numbered objects against shorter action stems.
# These existing particles must retain right context under short phrase targets.
# Route nouns win over recurring-time words that can also be route names.
# Direct attached distributive marker; identifier context still takes precedence.
# Frequency cues for 번 chosen from the Korean benchmark references (2026-10-05): at least
# five uses with 90% native readings (의 87%, 147 : 22). Identifier cues still outrank them.
# Route words keep a route number Sino even with a frequency tail (마을버스 32번의, 76번의 배차).
# Numbers in a list or a queue (37번과 38번의, 대기번호가 12번이나) are identifiers.
# 37번과 38번: after the first count is read, its particle stands alone before the next number.
# Event verbs after N번: a count, native numeral (3번 말했다 세 번; 2026-10-08).
# Laps and climbs after N번 (운동장을 20번 돌았다 스무 번; 2026-11-02, TN round 32).
# Errors after N번 are counts too (5번 틀려서, 5번 오류로; 2026-10-08).
